title: Unable to open a script with external code editor when internal script editor is off.
body:
### Tested versions

-Reproducible in: 4.5.1-stable, 4.6-stable, latest commit in master branch as of 2026-02-01_2:52PM-PST (commit: 98782b6c8c9cabe0fb7c80bc62640735ecb076d3)

### System information

Godot v4.6.stable.mono.double (89cea1439) - CachyOS Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Sat, 24 Jan 2026 21:21:21 +0000 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 SUPER (nvidia; 590.48.01) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-10400F CPU @ 2.90GHz (12 threads) - 11.54 GiB memory

### Issue description

I wanna make it clear you _can_ open a script in an external code editor by right-clicking and clicking on: "Open In External Program", however, you're unable to _double-click_ on a script to open it in an external editor when the internal script editor button is visibly off.

I find it to be an eye-sore having the internal script editor being toggled on.

How I think it should work, is that when turning off the script editor and having an external editor setup, it should _not_ require the internal script editor to be toggled on to open a script.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Go to: Editor > Editor Settings > Text Editor > External (Have Advanced Settings toggled on)
2. Change Exec Path to:
```
/usr/bin/codium (or whatever external editor you use)
```
3. (For VSCode/Codium) Change Exec Flags to:
```
{project} --goto {file}:{line}:{col}
```
4. Toggle on:  Use External Editor
5. Go to: Editor > Manage Editor Features
6. Toggle off: Script Editor
7. Create and attempt to open a new gdscript file by double-clicking
